title: Evidence on the Use and Efficacy of International Whistleblowing Systems

scopes.description: Complete author-supplied workflow embedded in JAR Code.pdf: getdata.sas, prepare.do, tables12.do and tables345.do, including the supplied descriptive, figure and table analyses. The document is not a directly executable complete driver; no compatible author-prepared analysis dataset is supplied, so the processing stages remain in scope.

requirements.description: Two NAVEX report CSVs are imported, cleaned, categorized, appended and restricted to matched firm-years. Code reads clientid, client, reportdate, dateclosed, issue, outcome or resolution, source, length, reporter, intakemethod, anonymous, mgtaware, mgtinvolved and accesscount. The CSVs are not supplied; the code does not bound their raw dates, while Tables 1–5 analyze firm-years 2004–2017.

issues.description: The embedded SAS listing includes external winsorize.sas and references &testc without a visible definition. Their macro body and macro-variable expansion are unprovided. COMP/CRSP librefs and document path placeholders are ordinary runtime configuration choices and can be set coherently when transcribing the supplied programs.

The package suppresses 21 of 22 manual clientid corrections and both masked_id calculations; the datasheet also withholds a firm identifier list under the NAVEX NDA. These are not inferable from public identifiers. Obtain the exact authorized secure workflow/crosswalk and formulas or a compatible author-prepared input route.

The second CSV merges resolution into outcomecat, but the later keep statement also requests outcome. The package does not establish whether the second CSV contains outcome or whether a specific field/line is incomplete. Clarify its exact schema and preserve the two distinct outcome mappings.

The required penalties file is read but no code produces it. Its CIK/FYEAR mapping, LOGNPEN/LOGDPEN construction, time shift and history cannot be inferred; Appendix A5 describes fine outcomes at t+1 to t+3, while the visible merge is same-FYEAR. Request the author producer or exact prepared file and its construction documentation.

The kldscores file is read but no producer is included. The available KLD.HISTORY candidate contains raw item fields, while exact category aggregation, output suffixes, CUSIP6/FYEAR construction and alignment are undocumented. Do not reconstruct the scores from catalog labels alone.

The legal input KEEP list requests CASE_START_DATE_S but excludes DOCK_NUM; subsequent code sorts by DOCK_NUM. The locally probed Feed14 candidate has CASE_START_DATE without the _S suffix. Confirm the intended author table/schema and the correct retained key before preparing a compatible source.

The code expects na_wrds_company_names, while the catalog candidate that has COMPANYID/BOARDID/CIKCODE is na_wrds_org_summary. Product and alias equivalence are not established; obtain the exact intended table or a documented compatible mapping.

The ownership code reads an undeclared, unqualified NAMES table requiring NCUSIP/CUSIP. COMP.NAMES lacks NCUSIP in the catalog; CRSP.STOCKNAMES contains it but is not established as the intended source. Confirm the actual library, table and matching rule.

The SAS assignment size = log(at) is missing its statement terminator before the next asterisk comment. Inserting a semicolon in the extracted working copy is a directly supported syntax repair; the binary PDF remains unchanged.

AuditAnalytics. It saves the final dataset as a Stata .dta file, which we merge to the internal

evidence.description: The author documents prepare.do and its report-level and firm-year outputs, then the two supplied table programs.
evidence.quote:
whistleblowing data using “prepare.do”.

2. prepare.do

This Stata program accesses the internal whistleblowing data provided by NAVEX Global and
creates a number of variables that we use in the study. It merges the whistleblowing data with all
our other data, then creates two output files: “navdata_reports.dta” and “navdata_firmyear.dta”.
We use the former file in our report-level analyses presented in Tables 1 and 2, and we use the
latter file in our firm-year analyses presented in Tables 3 through 5.

3. tables12.do

The Stata program uses “navdata_reports.dta” to create Tables 1 and 2 of the published paper.

4. tables345.do

The Stata program uses “navdata_firmyear.dta” to create Tables 3 through 5 of the published
paper.

evidence.description: The SAS program includes an external winsor macro and defines product library paths; COMP and CRSP setup is not shown here.
Compustat annual data read, field contract, 2002–2018 filter and core transformations.
The Compustat company table supplies GICS group codes.
Annual lags and changes are conditioned on adjacent fiscal years.
The code reads geographic segment history and uses source-date selection to construct revenue dispersion.
CRSP link, return, volume and market-return reads; the return construction requires twelve monthly observations in the eleven months before through the fiscal date.
Firm age uses a separate Compustat history read with an unresolved macro; stocknames supplies date-effective SIC codes.
The supplied SAS macro call and parameters are not accompanied by the included macro file.
TFN S34 holdings and an unqualified NAMES table are used to construct institutional ownership.
AuditAnalytics legal events are filtered through 2018, but the KEEP list and later DOCK_NUM sort disagree; the join aligns event year to fiscal year plus one.
AuditAnalytics internal-control fields are read and matched to current and prior fiscal-year dates.
BoardEx role dates and a company-name/CIK table are needed for the compliance-role indicator.
SAS-derived variables and legal-data missingness rules precede Stata export.
The first NAVEX CSV import, required fields and six category lookup merges.
evidence.quote:
* Import and prepare file #1

import delimited using "[redacted-path-d4d66fa681a1]", clear

* Clean variables
replace client    = strupper(stritrim(strtrim(client)))
replace issue     = strupper(stritrim(strtrim(issue)))
replace outcome = strupper(stritrim(strtrim(outcome)))
replace source    = strupper(stritrim(strtrim(source)))
replace length    = strupper(stritrim(strtrim(length)))
replace reporter = strupper(stritrim(strtrim(reporter)))
replace intakemethod = strupper(stritrim(strtrim(intakemethod)))

destring clientid, replace force

* Drop missing data
drop if missing(clientid)
drop if missing(client)
drop if missing(reportdate)
drop if missing(issue)

* Re-code dates
gen rdate = date(substr(reportdate,1,10),"YMD")
gen cdate = date(substr(dateclosed,1,10),"YMD")
format rdate %td
format cdate %td
drop reportdate dateclosed
gen year = year(rdate)

* Merge categories for issue type, outcome, and length using NAVEX mapping files
merge m:m issue using issuetypes, force keepusing(issuecat)
drop if _merge==2
drop _merge

merge m:m outcome using outcomes, force keepusing(outcomecat)
drop if _merge==2
drop _merge

merge m:m length using lengths, force keepusing(lengthcat)
drop if _merge==2
drop _merge

merge m:m source using sources, force keepusing(sourcecat)
drop if _merge==2
drop _merge

merge m:m reporter using reporters, force keepusing(reportercat)
drop if _merge==2
drop _merge

merge m:m intakemethod using intakes, force keepusing(intakecat)
drop if _merge==2
drop _merge

* Save dataset
keep clientid client rdate cdate year issue issuecat outcome outcomecat length lengthcat reporter reportercat
source sourcecat anonymous mgtaware mgtinvolved intakemethod intakecat accesscount
save navdata_temp, replace

* Create indicators for issue types
gen byte iss_ac = issuecat=="AC"

review_notes: The title and DOI are copied literally from the frozen output header. The attached datasheet uses the phrase Internal Whistleblowing Systems in its title; this assessment preserves that source identity while retaining the frozen International header.
The July 31, 2018 NAVEX transfer is an update date with a later end date, not a sample cutoff. The supplied analysis code explicitly keeps 2004–2017 firm-years.

The source data sheet documents actual signed NAVEX and Good Jobs First agreements and withheld sample identifiers. Those statements do not establish this user’s access or current data history. The current public Violation Tracker guide is only context; it is not evidence that the custom author-linked fines extract is equivalent.
The frozen dependency checklist is empty. Manual tracing of the document-embedded code found the requirements above; the empty parser output does not establish complete closure.
Only full_pipeline is retained. The package supplies no compatible prepared analysis data; analysis-only would require unavailable private data or undocumented intermediate producers.
The appendix is used only to clarify the documented t+1 to t+3 fines and t+1 legal outcomes; it does not add an unsupplied analysis program to the target.
Catalog probes are bounded one-row readability/column checks. They do not establish full source history, population fidelity or successful execution.

A self-written Stata 18 probe on in-memory synthetic rows confirmed that gen group5 = group(5) runs and creates five equal-count groups after sorting; repeated x values crossed boundaries in the synthetic example. The supplied source sorts by the target variable before calling it, so no replacement algorithm or issue is added.

The same Stata 18 synthetic probe confirmed that, with varabbrev on, accessco resolves to accesscount in gen, summarize and collapse, and the collapsed output remains named accesscount. The supplied code does not turn abbreviations off, so accessco is treated as a valid Stata abbreviation. This probe did not test winsor2, which remains a software preparation dependency.
The missing SAS statement terminator is proposed as a one-character insertion in the cached text working copy only; the binary JAR Code.pdf was not edited.
